content.comment_body: I'm using a 0-12 bar pressure sensor (4-20mA), and I need help adjusting the settings so the reading reflects 0.00 to 12.00 bar. Currently, Gain is 1.25 and Offset is -50.
Do you have an [product_name] analog expansion module, or are you trying to read the 4-20mA signal using a 0-10V input on the base module?
Yes, I have the analog expansion module. I connected the sensor but always get a value of 75, even without applying air pressure.
Can you share your program setup? Which analog input (AI) channel are you using?
The sensor is wired to the correct input. When a little pressure is applied, the value changes. Could the sensor be showing a non-zero reading due to atmospheric pressure?
Are you referring to the 0.83 mb value seen in your screenshot?
Yes!
Can you provide a drawing of how the sensor is wired? Also, do you have a link to the sensor specification?
It's a Danfoss AKS 33 060G2101. I just realized the range is -1 to 12 bar. Apologies for the mistake. The measuring range should be -100 to 1200, correct?
Yes, but to get correct values, you can’t use just an analog amplifier. A mathematical instruction is also required.
See screenshot for reference.
Thanks!
Has your issue been resolved now?
I'm still seeing a value of -0.09.

Have you considered that electrical components have inherent tolerances and errors? For [product_name], analog inputs have a ±1.5% error tolerance from the end of the measuring range. In your case, for a range of 16.25 bar, that's roughly ±0.24 bar. The sensor itself also has a tolerance.
You're right! Is it possible to round the value so it only changes by decimal steps, like +0.10, +0.20, etc.?

So you prefer a single decimal place instead of two? Note that this won't eliminate errors. If you display 0.1 instead of 0.09, the underlying issue remains. Maybe you want to correct the zero point instead? If so, adjust the value in parameter V4 from -425 to -416.
-414 worked. Now I want to turn off an output when the pressure is greater than 2 bar. Should the comparator use the value from the amplifier or from the mathematical block?
See the attached file. If pressure is below 1.9 bar, the compressor will turn on. If pressure is above 2.0 bar, the compressor remains off.
Is your issue resolved now?

analysis.insight_summary: The user is facing challenges configuring a 0-12 bar (4-20mA) pressure sensor with an analog expansion module to display accurate pressure readings. The discussion includes troubleshooting for calibration parameters, explaining sensor signals at atmospheric pressure, and ensuring correct scaling. Recommendations cover wiring verification, correct scaling formulas, error tolerance, and logic for output control based on measured pressure.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the system to provide an accurate, scalable pressure readout matching the sensor's range—specifically, showing zero bar at atmospheric pressure and 12 bar at maximum—along with reliable control outputs triggered by specific pressure thresholds.
